findings.reason: §4 would drop the new-axis proposal and query the existing edge, which is the reuse map re-run over the one section the plan did not search.
findings.text: §4 states "Nothing marks one as a member of a component set, so a missing component is invisible to every reader", but `imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:7044` populates `("component", "HAS_COMPONENT")` from the parsed `component` segment, `imas_codex/schemas/standard_name.yaml:1664` declares the `grammar_component_token` slot, and `imas_codex/standard_names/families.py:196` (`detect_families`) already returns a `VectorFamily` whose `family_type` is `physical_vector` vs `geometric_coordinate`; the plan's only reuse citation is `HAS_PARENT`, so its premise is falsified by an existing owner it did not cite

findings.reason: naming the owning edge turns §4 from a schema addition into a completeness query, shrinking its scope and removing a permanent second component dimension.
findings.text: the decision `component-is-a-family-axis` ("a vector component becomes a distinguished dimension of the name family in the graph schema") and §4's "the component axis is added to the GRAPH schema" re-implement a distinction the `HAS_COMPONENT` typed edge (owner: `graph_ops.py:_SEGMENT_EDGE_TYPES` + `schemas/standard_name.yaml`), and should extend/query that owner rather than fork a second axis; the plan's own comment already concedes the completeness query "is expressible today"

findings.reason: the stale §5 step would spend catalogue-release surface on a field the plan's own decision retired, which the author can delete or reword in one line.
findings.text: §5 step 5 requires the axis "carried into `catalog.yml` so the published sidecar exposes the family grouping the site needs", but the locked decision `the-name-is-the-decomposition` retracts exactly this ("the published catalog needs NO segment-decomposition field; the site … decomposes each name itself; the catalog side needs only the right package pin"), so §4/§5 duplicate derivable state the site already computes and that the plan elsewhere records as the drift defect class it keeps closing

findings.reason: §9 already lands the withdrawal, so this is a stale §7 heading rather than a live decision to reverse; it matters only as an instruction not to re-open the token in the release that §7 and §9 jointly own.
findings.text: §7 lists "an iron-core β token" as a vocabulary gap and admits `beta_inclination` as a geometry qualifier, but §9 withdraws it because `beta_angle_of_ferritic_element`/`beta_angle_of_passive_loop` were superseded in favour of `tilt_angle_`/`vertical_angle_`; §7 offers no reason the existing angle machinery cannot carry the meaning, which is the justification `thin_wrapper` requires

findings.reason: the section must either name the retirement (as the `the-name-is-the-decomposition` decision already did) or drop the field; left as written it reads as a sanctioned budget addition.
findings.text: against the week's `public_definitions 0`, §5 adds a published-sidecar field (`catalog.yml` family-grouping) without naming in the section what it retires or why nothing can be, and it is the one place the plan would grow an interface family the budget reports at zero

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the locked decision `rendering-rule-not-a-rename-pass` declines the thin prompt wrapper and places the behaviour once in the renderer/grammar, with parse→re-render→supersede as the single migration path; the complexity sits behind one authority rather than a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4/§5 propose adding a component axis to the graph schema and carrying it into `catalog.yml`, duplicating the axis already owned by the `HAS_COMPONENT` typed edge and, on the catalog side, a derivable fact the plan's own decision `the-name-is-the-decomposition` rules out shipping.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §5 adds a `catalog.yml` sidecar field to the published sidecar without naming in the section what it retires or why nothing can be, and the section text contradicts the plan's own retraction of that field.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §4 asserts nothing in the graph marks a name as a member of a component set, but the graph already carries `(StandardName)-[:HAS_COMPONENT]->(GrammarToken)` and `imas_codex/standard_names/families.py::detect_families` already partitions component variants from qualifier variants; the plan cites only `HAS_PARENT`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §7 admits `beta_inclination` as a new vocabulary token over the existing angle base without consulting the superseded population, so it is a parallel token where an existing spelling (`tilt_angle`/`vertical_angle`) was already the project's answer.
